fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark or label both detached structures from the access drive so responders can quickly identify which structure they are approaching.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and each detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Trim any vegetation that has grown against or directly alongside the detached structures, keeping a clear gap between plants and exterior walls.
• Identify the rear access point and keep it unlocked or secured with a method that allows quick forced entry.
• Mark any rear gate or access point with a visible sign or reflective indicator so responders can locate it without circling the property.
• Keep both vehicle parking areas clear of stored equipment or materials that would block responder staging space.
• Trim any landscaped plantings that narrow or obstruct the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of vehicles, trailers, or debris that would prevent a fire or medical unit from reaching the rear of the property.
• Cut back any vegetation along the perimeter fencing that would prevent responders from locating or opening fence access points.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that have grown close to any structure walls or foundations.
• Thin scattered trees near structures to increase open space between tree canopy and rooflines.
• Mow or cut grass across open terrain areas close to structures before dry season.
• Keep grass cut short in areas between shrub groupings and structures.
• Maintain clear, unobstructed travel along all driveway and access routes through the property.
• Remove dead grass and dried plant material that has accumulated near structures.
• Separate shrub groupings that are growing toward each other and toward structures to reduce connected patches of vegetation.
